## What The Business Is
Microsoft Corp. is a global technology company organized into three reportable segments: **Productivity and Business Processes**, **Intelligent Cloud**, and **More Personal Computing**. Its portfolio spans enterprise software subscriptions, cloud infrastructure, AI services, developer tools, business applications, LinkedIn, Windows, devices, search advertising, and gaming. In FY2025, Microsoft reported $281.7 billion of revenue and $128.5 billion of operating income, with Microsoft Cloud revenue of $168.9 billion. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/investor/reports/ar25/index.html?msockid=3db7fb97e7db61db1f89ed61e6d8602e))

## What It Does
In **Productivity and Business Processes**, Microsoft sells Microsoft 365 Commercial and Consumer, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams, Exchange, SharePoint, Security and Compliance, LinkedIn, and Dynamics 365. In **Intelligent Cloud**, it sells Azure and other cloud services, cloud/AI consumption services, GitHub cloud services, Nuance, virtual desktop, Windows Server, SQL Server, Visual Studio, and enterprise services. In **More Personal Computing**, it sells Windows OEM licensing, Surface/devices, Xbox hardware and content, Game Pass, Bing/Copilot search and news advertising, and Edge-related services. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/investor/reports/ar25/index.html?msockid=09fe5543d85b694b22f743a9d91e684a))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)
Microsoft’s April 29, 2026 FY26 Q3 results were strong: revenue was $82.9 billion, up 18%; operating income was $38.4 billion, up 20%; and diluted EPS was $4.27, up 23% on a GAAP basis. Management said Microsoft Cloud revenue was $54.5 billion, up 29%, and Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 40%, with demand still exceeding available capacity. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/fy-2026-q3/press-release-webcast))

AI commercialization accelerated in the transcript period: Microsoft said its AI business surpassed a $37 billion annual revenue run rate, up 123% year over year; Microsoft 365 Copilot paid seats exceeded 20 million; and M365 Commercial Cloud revenue grew 19%. Management also cited over 35,000 paid Fabric customers and broad enterprise agent adoption in the provided call excerpt. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/fy-2026-q3/press-release-webcast))

Recent platform news reinforced the AI/cloud strategy. At Build 2026, Microsoft highlighted broader model choice and said Fireworks AI was generally available on Foundry with enterprise governance and Azure data residency; in June, Microsoft also announced a new Pecos, Texas datacenter intended to expand AI-era capacity. ([blogs.microsoft.com](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/06/02/microsoft-build-2026-be-yourself-at-work/))

## Bull Case
- Revenue momentum is exceptional for a company this size: +18% in FY26 Q3, Microsoft Cloud +29%, Azure +40%, with demand still exceeding capacity.
- AI monetization is real: $37B AI run-rate (+123% y/y), 20M+ paid Copilot seats, 35K+ paid Fabric customers — supporting durable double-digit growth and eventual FCF inflection once capex normalizes.
- Net income TTM jumped ~30% y/y ($96.6B → $125.2B), showing strong underlying earnings power masked in FCF by AI datacenter investment.
- In a bull scenario, capex intensity plateaus while cloud/AI revenue compounds, letting FCF re-accelerate toward 12–15% growth and justifying a premium 42–45x EV/FCF, implying EV well above $3.3T.

## Bear Case
- FCF is nearly stagnant: $70.6B (2024) → $69.4B (2025) → $72.9B (2026), only ~3% CAGR despite ~16% revenue CAGR — AI capex is consuming incremental cash.
- The primer flags AI growth "coming with margin" pressure; further datacenter buildouts (e.g., Pecos, TX) suggest capex stays elevated through the forecast horizon.
- Current EV/FCF of ~40x is rich versus the 3-year average FCF/EV yield (~2.24%, i.e., ~45x — but yield volatility shows sentiment risk). Any AI monetization disappointment or capacity overbuild could compress the multiple to 32–34x, implying EV closer to $2.5–2.6T.
- Market cap 3y history shows ~12.6% standard deviation; drawdown risk is material.

## Logic
- **Forward FCF:** TTM FCF is $72,916M. Revenue is growing ~18% but capex absorbs most of it; recent FCF growth was ~5% y/y. I assume modest capex-intensity stabilization plus strong revenue growth yields ~8% FCF growth: **forward FCF ≈ $78,750M**.
- **Applied multiple:** Current EV/FCF = $2,913,333M / $72,916M ≈ 40.0x. Given continued margin/capex pressure, I apply a slight discount at **38.0x EV/FCF**, still a premium multiple warranted by AI-driven growth durability.
- **Forward EV:** 78,750 × 38.0 = **$2,992,500M**.
- **EV → Market cap bridge:** Current EV − market cap gap = 2,913,332.6 − 2,888,472.6 = $24,860M (net debt). Forward market cap = 2,992,500 − 24,860 ≈ **$2,967,640M**.
- Sanity check: ~+2.7% vs. current market cap ($2.89T), and within the 3-year mean ($3.13T) minus ~0.4 std — a reasonable central estimate balancing strong growth against FCF stagnation.

Azure (+40%) and AI run-rate ($37B, +123% YoY) sustain ~15-18% revenue growth. FCF, currently depressed by heavy AI capex, begins to inflect as datacenter buildout matures. This pushes EV well above $3.7T and market cap toward $3.75T+.

FCF stays roughly flat or grows only low-single-digits (~$74,000M) while the multiple derates toward the historical average (~40x current implied inverse of 2.5% FCF/EV yield reverting to ~2.2% avg = ~45x).
